Control engineering / Energy measurement

Dual-Axis
Solar Tracking and Real-Time Energy
Performance Monitoring

A panel that follows the light. A separate instrument that measures what it produces.

Four light sensors guide an STM32 controller. An ESP32 records voltage, current, and energy through an INA226. This is the design, the hardware, and the evidence behind the comparison.

Hardware, explained

Every component
has a specific role.

Select a part to inspect what it measures, controls, or carries. Pin mappings and limitations are part of the design.

Control processor

STM32G031K8

Reads four light dividers, filters each channel, and converts imbalance into bounded pan and tilt commands. Network traffic is handled by the other board.

Inputs
PA4, PA1, PA5, PA0 / ADC1
Outputs
PA8 and PA10 / TIM1 PWM
Control target
5 ms per update; timing needs hardware verification
Measurement boundary

The feedback variable is light imbalance. Servo pulse width does not measure panel angle.

Understanding the metrics

Power is a rate.
Energy accumulates.

The logger integrates valid power samples over actual elapsed time. A measurement gap is excluded rather than filled with an assumed reading.

Constant-power calculation

Calculated energy0.2500 Wh

A mathematical example at constant power. It does not describe a recorded solar session.

Electrical power

P = V × I

Voltage multiplied by current at the monitored node. The fixed load defines the operating point.

Rated-power utilization

100 × P / 0.9 W

Output relative to the configured panel rating. This is not solar conversion efficiency.

Gross and net energy

100 × (Etracked − Efixed) / Efixed

Gross gain compares panel output. Net benefit would also require measured actuator and control consumption.

What this project establishes

Light-feedback control, timed electrical acquisition, session recording, and measured power and energy results.

The experiments measured panel electrical output in sequential sessions. Solar conversion efficiency and net energy benefit require additional irradiance and actuator-energy measurements.
